candidate.title: Compare decimals with equal units
prerequisiteAssumptions: Recognize tens and ones in whole numbers.

misconceptions.description: The decimal with more digits must be larger.
misconceptions.response: Express both decimals with the same place units before comparing.

scenes.title: compare: intro
scenes.learnerAction: Read the explanation and describe the place units in your own words.

content.body: We will compare decimals and justify which has greater value without counting digits.

accessibility.textAlternative: We will compare decimals and justify which has greater value without counting digits.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Read the paragraph in document order.

offline.note: Use the text and a notebook; capture written responses for later sync.

scenes.title: compare: model
scenes.learnerAction: Read the explanation and describe the place units in your own words.

content.body: Compare 0.6 and 0.48. Six tenths is sixty hundredths. Sixty hundredths is greater than forty-eight hundredths, so 0.6 is greater.

accessibility.textAlternative: Compare 0.6 and 0.48. Six tenths is sixty hundredths. Sixty hundredths is greater than forty-eight hundredths, so 0.6 is greater.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Read the paragraph in document order.

offline.note: Use the text and a notebook; capture written responses for later sync.

content.body: Rewrite 0.7 as hundredths. Now compare it with 0.65. Explain the common unit you chose.

accessibility.textAlternative: Rewrite 0.7 as hundredths. Now compare it with 0.65. Explain the common unit you chose.

scenes.title: compare: misconception
scenes.learnerAction: Read the explanation and describe the place units in your own words.

content.body: Counting decimal digits does not compare their value. For 0.5 and 0.42, think fifty hundredths and forty-two hundredths. Adding a trailing zero changes notation but not quantity.

accessibility.textAlternative: Counting decimal digits does not compare their value. For 0.5 and 0.42, think fifty hundredths and forty-two hundredths. Adding a trailing zero changes notation but not quantity.

scenes.title: compare: independent
scenes.learnerAction: Which is greater, 0.8 or 0.76? Justify using equal units.

content.body: Work alone without a place chart, tutor or worked example. Explain the units used in your comparison.
